AlternateTargets: return home by way of the road
Senses.Explanation: As a public Chan appraisal, ‘take the road home’ judges a person or saying by the homeward-road image. The records apply and contest the verdict in encounters; this sense does not silently absorb an ordinary physical journey. Literally the phrase says ‘take the road and return home.’
Senses.Note: No single master-specific sense is warranted. The phrase occurs across many late records, often with “turn around and return to the father” or the reversed “leave home and take the road.” The article reports those textual relations without assigning a spiritual force to “home.”

Senses.Note: Exact concordance: 75 matches in 37 allowlisted texts. Frequent family forms include “Xu You washes his ears” (17 matches in 15 texts), “Xu You does not wash his ears” (12/9), and “Xu You discards the gourd” (4/3); Chaofu appears 40 times in 29 texts. One figure sense: washing, not washing, refusing the realm, and discarding the gourd all refer to Xu You. Mount Ji, Chaofu, the ox, and the gourd are related allusion elements, not additional Xu You senses.

Senses.Explanation: Xu You, the recluse whom the Chan corpus identifies through Yao's offer of the realm, retirement at Mount Ji, washing his ears, and discarding his gourd. Wansong's commentary supplies the story in brief: Xu You lived hidden at Mount Ji, Yao yielded the imperial position to him, and Xu You washed his ears at the river after hearing it. Juelang Daosheng adds that Xu You feared being burdened by possession of the realm and would rather die than accept it. The records then put those acts into public exchanges. Jingqing answers a request for direction to what is finest before sound with “Xu You did not wash his ears,” and says washing would still leave his feet tied. Another fourfold host-and-guest exchange answers “What is the host within the guest?” with “Xu You washes his ears.” Baoning Renyong directly appraises the inherited image: Xu You's ear-washing merely displays lofty purity, while Chaofu's watering of the ox merely flaunts spirit. Hongzhi's portrait verse retains another part of the family, “Xu You discarded the gourd.” The Zen deviation is therefore observable rather than honorific: a classical refusal figure is made an answer, assigned a place in host-and-guest grammar, negated, and openly criticized from the teaching seat.

Senses.Explanation: “Flourishing yellow flowers” travels with the proposition that yellow flowers are wisdom, and the records preserve both affirmation, rejection, and interview testing of that formula. Literally, flourishing or luxuriant yellow flowers : "flourishing yellow flowers." The phrase occurs 57 times in 41 allowlisted texts. Its distinctively Chan deployment is the frequently quoted proposition, "the green bamboo is entirely the body of the teaching; the flourishing yellow flowers are nothing other than wisdom" . The fuller exact yellow-flower formula occurs 18 times in , while "green bamboo" occurs 116 times in 68. The records preserve disagreement rather than a single unopposed gloss. A question to National Teacher Huizhong says that some call the proposition an erroneous saying while others trust it as inconceivable; his recorded answer accepts it by placing bamboo and flowers within the range of the teaching body and wisdom. The same transmitted passage then has a Huayan lecturer ask Dazhu Huihai why he does not permit the formula; Dazhu distinguishes appearing in response to bamboo and flowers from wisdom or the teaching body being located in those objects. Later, Shending Yikui rebukes people who hear the formula, hold rigidly to it, and never shift at all, calling a fitting phrase "a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand ages" . In another exchange he asks how wisdom is understood when the yellow flowers are right here, and tells the respondent that he has let the yellow flowers down. Chan thus bends a scene of colored plants into a portable, disputed proposition and a live examination question; this entry reports the acceptance, distinction, and correction recorded by the texts without deciding among them.
